literal: Even if one does painful things like the touch of a cluster of fire, if possible, not getting angry is good.
translation: Even if someone inflicts painful harms as agonizing as being touched by a blazing fire, it is best, if one can manage it, to refrain from anger.
modern: நெருப்புக் கூட்டத்தைத் தொடுவது போன்ற துன்பங்களை ஒருவன் நமக்குச் செய்தாலும், முடிந்தவரை அவனிடம் கோபம் கொள்ளாமல் இருப்பது நல்லது.
explanation: The couplet highlights the supreme value of patience and anger management under extreme provocation. The poet compares severe, malicious harm to the physical agony of being touched by a blazing, multi-tongued fire ('இணர் எரி'). Even when subjected to such intense pain, the author advises that if one can possibly summon the strength ('புணரின்'), remaining free from anger ('வெகுளாமை') is the best course of action. This emphasizes that self-control is not just for minor annoyances but is most crucial and noble during the most severe trials.
